title: Adaptation of a Haptic Robot in a 3T fMRI
protocol: Place the rolling table with the free end supported and the exterior end of the long handle detached.
Check that the robot is switched off.
Place the robot in the table socket.
Secure the aluminum safety plate over the robot with 2 screws.
Attach the end effector to the robot handle with the aluminum adapter.
Check that the end effector moves freely.
Attach the 10' parallel cable with aluminum shielding to the robot.
Check that the shielding is intact.
Add extra foil if needed.
Place the aluminum shielding box over the robot, being careful to place the parallel and power cables into the groove on the back.
Carefully screw on the shielding box.
Pack aluminum foil into the cable groove on the shielding box.
Ensure the foil makes contact with the shielding on the parallel cable.
Remove any metallic objects including non-ferrous ones before entering a high magnetic field environment.
With person A holding the free end of the robot table and person B stabilizing the box end, roll it free end first until the robot just enters the door of the room.
Person B clips the security rope tethered to an anchor hole on the back of the shielding case.
Check that the other end is firmly attached to a wall anchor.
Roll the table into the room.
Attach the table with Velcro straps to the foot of the fMRI table.
Attach the robot's parallel cable to the custom filter on the pass through.
Plug in the robot.
Make sure the shielding foil on the parallel cable contacts the filter.
Attach the exterior part of the long handle (end effector).
Verify that the end effector will enter the bore of the fMRI cleanly.
Start the control computer.
Attach the 6' parallel cable to the robot.
Remove any extra filters from the interior part of the pass through.
Verify that the robot motors are turned off.
Start up the Phantom calibration routine.
Check that position readouts of the motors from the robot's calibration routine are stable.
Double check the parallel cable connection if the calibration routine cannot see the robot or there are large variations in motor readout.
Open the port on the back of the shielding box with a stick to turn on the robot.
Press the switches inside the shielding box with a stick.
Restart the calibration routine with the end effector centered at the end of the conical waveguide.
Step through the calibration and check that the haptic interaction is appropriate in the box calibration.
Attach the TTL output from the fMRI (BNC connector) to the Labjack ADC on the control computer.
Prepare the subject for a high magnetic field environment with standard fMRI protocols.
Set up any extra equipment for the experiment.
Use the NordicNeuro Lab, Inc. Vision System for stereo viewing of visual displays.
Have the subject lie down on the table and position the head coil.
Loosen the hand screws to adjust the distance of the robot.
Slide the top of the table until the subject can move comfortably.
Guide the fMRI table manually while moving in and out of the bore.
Ensure the end effector goes into the bore without catching on the outside.
Run the experiment.
Remove the exterior end of the long handle after the patient exits.
Detach the robot table from the fMRI table by undoing the Velcro strap.
From the robot, disconnect the shielded parallel cable and power cable.
Have person A hold the free end of the robot table.
With person B guiding the robot end, move the table to the door.
At the door, unplug the tether and roll the robot table out to the hall.
Undo all screws from the shielding box and remove the robot.
Double check the aluminum shielding on the cable for proper placement and filtering.
Place a ferrous core properly on the parallel cable near the robot.
Ensure that the only filter applied is the custom filter on the scanner room side of the pass-through.
Tighten all screws on the robot table, especially the hand adjustment screws.
Take an anatomical scan early in the study to check for zipper effects or other artifacts indicative of correlated noise.
